title: What you remember isn't what's likely
hook: You're scared of planes and relaxed in cars. The statistics laugh at you.
caption: Easy to remember feels likely. The availability heuristic makes us fear rare, dramatic events and ignore the boring risks that actually get us. Look up the frequency.

headline: SCARED OF
THE WRONG
THING.

scenes.say: You're scared of planes and relaxed in cars. The statistics laugh at you.
The availability heuristic: if it's easy to remember, it feels likely.
Rare, shocking events get covered for days. Common dangers barely make the news.
Memory measures how vivid something is, not how often it happens.
So we fear the dramatic and ignore the boring stuff that actually gets us.
When you judge a risk, find the real frequency, not the first example in your head.

takeaway: When you judge a risk, find the real frequency, not the first example in your head.
